answer:
The second most powerful earthquake ever recorded was the **1964 Great Alaska earthquake** (also known as the Good Friday earthquake), which measured **magnitude 9.2** on the moment magnitude scale. 

This earthquake resulted in approximately **130 deaths**. Most of these fatalities were caused by the tsunami that followed the initial seismic event rather than the shaking itself, although some people did die from direct earthquake effects. The majority of the damage occurred in Anchorage and other parts of south-central Alaska, while also affecting coastal areas where the tsunami struck.
